cohort: The study included 150 pregnancies diagnosed with intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) according to Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine guidelines.
finding: The presence of umbilical-portal-systemic venous shunts in fetuses with IUGR is associated with earlier IUGR diagnosis and delivery, an increased risk for fetal death, a different Doppler flow pattern, and additional congenital vascular anomalies.
cross-section timing: At the time of intrauterine growth restriction diagnosis, with detailed anomaly and targeted portal system scans performed then.
gest_age: Mean gestational age at IUGR diagnosis was 29.7 ± 5.6 weeks (study group) vs 32.47 ± 4.6 weeks (control group); mean gestational age at delivery was 33.50 ± 6.0 weeks (study group) vs 36.13 ± 2.8 weeks (control group).
